title: Handheld spot and strip instrument
summary: An instrument you hold in your hand: you place it on one patch (spot) or slide it along a row of patches (strip), with or without a ruler.
experience_text: This list is built from real sessions: owners of an i1Pro, i1Pro 2, i1Pro 3 and ColorMunki recorded X-Rite's programs with the earlier X-Rite recording tool, and every block below answers a question that cost us an extra round when it was missing (lights, the ruler, dual scan, the measurement conditions M0, M1 and M2, refused strips, calibration).
before_you_start: Your instrument, its USB cable and its calibration tile or cap.
The program you normally measure with, closed for now.
One printed test chart that your program can read, with at least one row of 10 or more patches.
If your program uses a ruler or a backing board for strips: have it ready.
Unplug other USB devices you can do without (disks, memory sticks, phones, printers). A keyboard and a mouse may stay.

blocks.label: start
blocks.title: Plug in and start the program
steps: Make sure the measuring program is closed and the instrument is unplugged.
Start this block (the recording starts now).
Plug the instrument in.
Start the measuring program.
Wait until the program shows the instrument as connected, then wait 15 seconds more without touching anything.
blocks.note: Did the program find the instrument by itself? Did it show anything about the instrument (model, firmware, serial)? What did the instrument's lights do?
blocks.why: The first conversation is where the program identifies the instrument and reads its memory, and it is the one ChromIQ must repeat every time.

blocks.label: calibrate
blocks.title: Calibrate
steps: Start this block.
Start the calibration in the program, exactly as you normally do (white tile, or the instrument's calibration position).
Wait until the program says the calibration is done.
blocks.note: How long did it take? Did the program ask you to move a dial, place the instrument on a tile, or press a button? What did the lights do?
blocks.why: Calibration is the first thing ChromIQ must do right, and its timing and commands differ between models.

blocks.label: strip
blocks.title: One strip at your normal speed
steps: Start this block.
In the program, start reading a strip (a row of patches).
Read one row at your normal speed, from where you usually start.
Wait until the program has accepted the strip.
blocks.note: Which row, and from which end? Which measurement condition did the program show (M0, M1, M2, dual scan, or none)? What did the lights do before, during and after?
blocks.why: This is the reading ChromIQ needs most often: how the program starts a strip, how the readings arrive, and how it decides the strip is good.

blocks.label: spot
blocks.title: One patch, three times (spot)
blocks.only_if: Skip this block if the program has no way to read one single patch.
steps: Start this block.
Switch the program to reading single patches (spot mode).
Read the same patch three times, lifting the instrument in between.
Switch the program back to strips if it does not do so by itself.
blocks.note: Did the program show numbers for each reading? Were they the same each time, or slightly different?
blocks.why: A spot reading has its own command, and three readings of one patch show whether the instrument does its own colour maths or sends raw sensor data.

blocks.label: strip-refused
blocks.title: A strip that fails on purpose
steps: Start this block.
Start a strip as in block H03.
Let it fail in one harmless way: lift the instrument halfway along the row, or move much too fast, or read the wrong row.
Read what the program says, and confirm its message.
If you like, do a second kind of failure the same way.
blocks.note: Which way did you make it fail? What exactly did the program say? Did the lights change?
blocks.why: Every ending must be known, not only the good one: how the instrument and the program report a bad strip decides what ChromIQ can tell its users.

blocks.label: cancel-reading
blocks.title: Cancel while reading
steps: Start this block.
Start a strip in the program.
While the instrument is reading (button pressed or reading under way), press Cancel or Stop in the program.
Wait until the program is ready again.
blocks.note: At which moment did you cancel? What did the program and the lights do?
blocks.why: A cancel in the middle of a reading is an ending ChromIQ must handle cleanly, and only a recording shows what the program sends then.

blocks.label: reference-chart
blocks.title: A small chart to the end, saved
steps: Start this block.
Read a small chart (or two or three rows of your chart) to the end, the normal way.
Save the measurement in the program (for example as a CGATS or text file), under a name you will recognise.
Keep that saved file: please send it together with the zip.
blocks.note: The name of the file you saved, and which rows you read.
blocks.why: A recording paired with the program's own result of that very measurement lets us check every number; a file saved another day cannot be paired.

blocks.label: dual-scan
blocks.title: The same strip in dual scan
blocks.only_if: Only if the program offers dual scan (i1Pro 2, i1Pro 3 and others).
steps: Start this block.
Switch the program to dual scan (or the mode that reads M0, M1 and M2 at once).
Read the row of block H03 as the program asks (often twice: forward and back). Type pass 1 and pass 2 when you start each pass.
blocks.note: How many passes did the program ask for, and what did the lights do?
blocks.why: A dual scan uses its own commands and a second pass, and ChromIQ can only offer it once it has seen them.

blocks.label: conditions
blocks.title: Each measurement condition on its own
blocks.only_if: Only the conditions the program offers (M0, M1, M2, UV cut, polarisation).
steps: Start this block.
For each condition the program offers: switch to it, type its name and press Enter, and read the row of block H03.
blocks.note: The conditions you tried, in order.
blocks.why: Each condition may be its own command or its own pass.

blocks.label: no-ruler
blocks.title: The same strip without the ruler
blocks.only_if: Only if the program offers reading with and without a ruler or backing board.
steps: Start this block.
Switch the program to reading without the ruler (if it has a setting for it), and read the row of block H03 freehand.
blocks.note: Did the program accept it?
blocks.why: Some instruments read the ruler's position; a strip without it shows what the program does when that data is missing.

blocks.label: other-modes
blocks.title: Every other reading mode
blocks.only_if: Only the modes your program offers that the blocks before did not cover.
steps: Start this block.
For each other way of reading the program offers (for example patch recognition on or off), type its name, press Enter and read one strip.
blocks.note: The modes you tried, in order.
blocks.why: Each mode may use its own commands.

blocks.label: strip-reverse
blocks.title: The same strip from the other end
steps: Start this block.
Read the row of block H03 again, but starting from the other end.
Wait until the program has accepted or refused it.
blocks.note: Did the program accept the strip read backwards?
blocks.why: Whether a strip may be read in both directions, and how the program tells, changes how ChromIQ checks a strip.

blocks.label: strip-fast
blocks.title: The same strip, clearly faster
steps: Start this block.
Read the row of block H03 again, clearly faster than normal (but not so fast that you expect a failure).
Wait until the program has accepted or refused it.
blocks.note: Accepted or refused? About how many seconds did the row take?
blocks.why: The readings per second and per patch, and the speed limit, come only from strips at different speeds.

blocks.label: strip-slow
blocks.title: The same strip, slowly
steps: Start this block.
Read the row of block H03 again, about twice as slowly as normal (count the seconds).
Wait until the program has accepted or refused it.
blocks.note: Accepted or refused? About how many seconds did the row take?
blocks.why: Together with H10 this shows how the instrument copes with speed, which decides ChromIQ's own speed advice.

blocks.label: buttons-lights
blocks.title: The button and the lights
steps: Start this block.
With the program waiting for a reading, press the instrument's button once without placing it on a patch, and see what happens.
If the program has settings for sounds or lights, open them and look, without changing them.
blocks.note: What did the lights and the program do when you pressed the button?
blocks.why: The lights and the button are how an instrument talks to its user, and ChromIQ wants to use them the same way the maker's program does.

blocks.label: idle
blocks.title: Five quiet minutes
steps: Start this block.
Leave the program open and the instrument connected, and do nothing for five minutes.
If the program asks for a new calibration during that time, note it, but do not calibrate yet.
blocks.note: Did anything happen on its own (a message, a light, a sound)?
blocks.why: Programs often talk to an idle instrument (keep-alive, temperature, a calibration that expires), and ChromIQ must know what keeps the instrument happy.

blocks.label: cable-pull
blocks.title: Pull the cable and plug it back
steps: Start this block (the recording keeps going while the instrument is gone).
With the program open and idle, pull the instrument's USB cable.
Wait 10 seconds and read what the program says.
Plug the cable back in and wait until the program shows the instrument again (or says it cannot).
blocks.note: What did the program say when the cable was pulled, and when it came back? Did it ask for a new calibration?
blocks.why: A pulled cable is an ending ChromIQ must survive; the recording shows how the program finds the instrument again.

blocks.label: close
blocks.title: Close the program
steps: Start this block.
Close the measuring program the normal way.
Wait 10 seconds.
blocks.note: Did the instrument's lights change when the program closed?
blocks.why: What the program sends when it closes is what ChromIQ should send when it lets go of the instrument.

blocks.label: restart
blocks.title: The program ends unexpectedly, then starts again
steps: Start this block, with the program open and the instrument plugged in.
End the program by force (Windows: Task Manager, select the program, End task. Mac: Apple menu > Force Quit).
Start the measuring program again.
Wait until it shows the instrument, and calibrate if it asks you to.
blocks.note: Did it ask for a calibration this time? Did the instrument's lights change?
blocks.why: After an unexpected end the instrument is left as the program left it; how the program starts again from there is what ChromIQ needs after its own unexpected end.

blocks.label: unplug-mid-strip
blocks.title: Unplug the cable in the middle of a strip
steps: Start this block (the recording keeps going while the instrument is gone).
Start reading a strip, and halfway along the row pull the instrument's USB cable. Type pulled.
Wait 10 seconds, plug it back in (into the same port) and let the program find it again.
blocks.note: What did the program say, and did it want a new calibration?
blocks.why: An instrument that disappears in the middle of a reading is an ending ChromIQ must survive.

blocks.label: questions
blocks.title: A few questions
steps: No recording now. Answer the questions below; a short line each is fine.
questions: Which instrument is it exactly (model and, if you know it, its generation)?
Which program and which version did you use?
On which system (Windows, macOS, Linux, and which version)?
Does your program offer anything that these blocks did not cover? A short description helps us add it to this list.
blocks.why: The recording cannot say which program and version made it, and a missing block is best found by the person who uses the program.
